dossiers.title: COCOON
dossiers.summary: Evidence summary: 9 validated structured observations; consult observations and conflicts for supported findings.

observations.statement: The central puzzle system treats entire miniature worlds as portable orbs that can nest inside each other, changing object positions and puzzle dependencies.
Puzzles generally teach new nesting logic without text guidance, with an accessible early curve and more mind-bending late combinations; some find the problem solving too simple.
An exceptionally concise, directed adventure replaces dialogue and explicit quests with spatial progression through alien biomes and several inventive staged boss encounters.
Critics find returning spheres and switches across levels repetitive, often adding steps rather than new insights to familiar puzzle patterns.
Players frequently admire the surreal alien-organic imagery and layered environmental design even when they criticize the puzzle structure.
At roughly a few hours, the puzzle campaign is considered tightly paced by some but too short or monotonous by others, with little narrative exposition.
Its wordless mysterious setting leaves the story open to interpretation; some love discovery-based atmosphere while others miss emotional or plot context.
Boss puzzle sequences provide visual and mechanical changes between areas, though some players find their repeated final variations underwhelming.
The electronic soundtrack and satisfying seamless transitions are appreciated by many, though others find audio subdued and limited.

conflicts.statement: World-nesting puzzles feel ingeniously designed and approachable to some players but monotonous and mechanically underdeveloped to others.
A nearly wordless abstract story reinforces the mysterious atmosphere for some but creates an empty world with insufficient character and meaning for others.

dossiers.title: Troublemaker
dossiers.summary: Evidence summary: 10 validated structured observations; consult observations and conflicts for supported findings.

observations.statement: The game centers on schoolyard beat-em-up combat, short fight encounters, consumable items, counters and special moves, recalling Yakuza-inspired action.
The high-school fighting tournament and its Indonesian setting and cast create a distinct youthful comedy-and-friendship identity.
Some players criticize stiff attacks, inconsistent parry or item input, imprecise hit detection and unreliable targeting, whereas others find the brawler fights enjoyable.
Fights provide money and stats or special move upgrades, but some critics report weak progression incentives and a repetitive combat loop.
A brief story alternates fights with restricted-area roaming, cutscenes and chapter-specific minigames; it is not a full urban open-world sandbox.
The dialogue-heavy school drama divides players: humor and local references are enjoyed by some while others find excessive profanity, melodramatic pacing and weak voice delivery distracting.
Some players enjoy the variety of school minigames and boss fights, while others point to repeated enemy encounters and limited free-roam objectives.
Several 2023 player reports describe crashes, cutscene failures or uneven framerate; a current Steam hub discussion also mentions video playback lag without proving current prevalence.
One exact-app Russian community post asks for a fan Russian translation; the current store metadata does not list Russian text support, but the comment is not evidence of translated-text quality.
Players praise energetic music and attractive 2D character illustration, while some dislike the 3D rendering and mismatched character animation.

conflicts.statement: The culturally distinctive school brawler wins support for humor, music and its premise, but other players find the combat and dialogue under-polished.
For some players the school minigames and character interactions enrich the short story, whereas others find the repetitive fights and profanity crowd out satisfying play.

dossiers.title: Xuan-Yuan Sword 2
dossiers.summary: Evidence summary: 9 validated structured observations; consult observations and conflicts for supported findings.

observations.statement: The 1994 party-based RPG uses traditional turn-based fights, exploration, consumable magic and elemental interactions; fans value the classic systems while acknowledging their age.
Distinctive Chinese ink-painting aesthetics, mythological creatures and period soundtrack are frequently celebrated as foundational series characteristics.
Players highlight the more complete fantasy storyline, thematic lore and some narrative surprises, especially compared with its earlier series predecessor.
The original save system restricts saving to towns and some outdoor locations except with limited items or special objects, which players have needed community help to understand.
The Steam re-release runs through DOSBox; some buyers dislike the preservation-first packaging rather than a remade modern interface.
Equipment, elemental magic and the monster-refinement jar enable tactical adjustments as the adventure progresses, but the legacy design can require grinding.

English-speaking and Russian-origin players describe difficulty interpreting its Chinese-language menus, while some request an English translation; the available sources do not establish a current Russian-language player review.
The story proceeds along a mostly linear classic RPG adventure with random encounters, side routes and collectible secrets rather than free exploration.

Several reviews of the re-release are primarily nostalgic requests for other entries, offering limited detail about current-game play; feedback that addresses it praises its atmosphere while noting archaic conventions.

conflicts.statement: Preserving the original game's mythic world, music and classic mechanics brings nostalgia to fans, but aging controls and DOSBox packaging deter some modern players.
